correctness.rationale: On a finite rooted upper-Alexandrov tree, the envelope at vertex v is the minimum over the descendant subtree. The minimum of a sum equals the sum of minima if and only if all component functions share a minimizer. For atomless independent valuations the argmins are unique. Uniform random priority orders admit an independent decomposition into block interleavings and internal permutations. Their first-block choices at distinct vertices are thus mutually independent with weights 1/s_v and s_c/s_v. The k-way collision of complete subtree-argmin signatures is exactly the intersection of independent nodewise block-selector collision events, yielding the product formula. Chain and star specializations follow directly; full binary-tree exponential decay follows from a convergent geometric series. The included checker tests 462 exact fraction-valued collision instances at n<=6, k=2,3,4 and direct pointwise semantic equivalences at n<=3; these are corroboration, not the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact equality case of the affine-modal K inequality is naturally motivated by the July 2026 envelope semantics. The global event couples many overlapping descendant cones, so naive multiplication of individual-world probabilities is invalid. The proof resolves that dependence using uniform permutation interleavings and gives a structural all-tree, all-k invariant rather than a single small numerical case. It yields precise, meaningfully different asymptotic regimes (polynomial for paths/stars, exponential for perfect binary trees), a reusable quantitative boundary for the semantic inequality. It does not claim a general downstream completeness theorem.
